items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: I listened to, since I was a yeah little boy I listened to all the big bands, you know Tommy Dorsey etcetera etcetera.

ctx.x: stations and the gymnastics they had to go through with the antennas and all this. And I’m wondering about your experience.

Yeah well two things. One thing, my father was a doctor but he loved music. My whole paternal part of my family was totally musical. None of them are musicians but they all played for fun and they were doctors and professors. And my dad was a doctor and he loved big band music, he loved all kinds of American – I listened to, since I was a yeah little boy I listened to all the big bands, you know Tommy Dorsey etcetera etcetera. And Glenn Miller. He had everything. And up until when the embargo came, after that you…

That’s so interesting. I was wondering, because I was thinking of a question about that because from my standpoint the music that you were listening to, which I also loved, would be considered simpler than Cuban dance music and did that occur to you later on? That the music of your own country was more complex, or am I off base here?
